newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CYCLING-HEEB GIVES SWITZERLAND FIRST ROAD RACE TITLE IN 45 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-HEEB GIVES SWITZERLAND FIRST ROAD RACE TITLE IN 45 YEARS.

text.p: Barbara Heeb gave Switzerland their first victory in the women's world road race championship on Saturday, and their first world road race title for 45 years.
She shook off her Lithuanian rival Rasa Polikeviciute on the final climb of the Crespera mountain after dominating the 100.8-km race.
Her solo ride over the final five kms put her 16 seconds clear of Polikeviciute at the finish with Canadian Linda Jackson taking the bronze, 36 seconds later.
Switzerland's last world road title came in 1951 when Ferdi Kuebler won the professional event at Varese, Italy.
Heeb's powerful riding ended the hopes of Frenchwoman Jeannie Longo, the Olympic road race champion, who was seeking her 12th world crown.
The Swiss woman escaped at the foot of the Canobbio climb on the third of the six laps. One lap further on she had a lead of 53 seconds and only Jackson and Polikeviciute for company.
On a day when the mighty Longo was expected to rule, Heeb had other plans and only Polikeviciute held out the longest.
Jackson spent the last two laps fighting to stay with her co-leaders, rejoining them each time only to fall away on the next rain-dampened climb.
Longo trailed in one minute 51 seconds after Heeb, who was eighth in the Olympic race.
The five times world champion was seventh, tucked in a group from which American Laura Charameda snatched fourth from Polikeviciute's twin, Jolanda.
It was the second victory for the Swiss in these championships which end on Sunday with the 252 km men's race.
Among the 177 starters will be Switzerland's Alex Zuelle, winner of the world time trial championship on Thursday.
Heeb said: "I based my race around Longo, but when I attacked I did not realise at first that I had lost her. When I discovered that she had gone I imposed my own pace to maintain the lead.
"I wanted to make up for Atlanta. I went there well prepared but it did not come off."
Longo said: "The first two laps were easy and I did not want to make too much effort too early. Maybe I should have."
